topic.title: Learnability and Distribution-Dependent Sample Complexity
topic.overview: Learning theory asks which families of prediction problems can be solved from finite observations and how quickly error can decrease. This topic examines hypothesis-class structure, distribution-sensitive guarantees, sample compression, noise, and online or transductive settings. Small changes in what must hold uniformly can produce fundamentally different learning rates.
topic.whyItMatters: These distinctions explain why a problem may be learnable on favorable distributions yet difficult under a universal guarantee. They also separate the existence of a learner from an efficient implementation, and clean-data results from guarantees that survive corrupted observations.
topic.evolution: A 1989 analysis studies perceptron learning under particular distributional protocols. Later representatives connect learnability with geometric and combinatorial dimensions. In 2025, marginal-nonuniform learning characterizes rates when guarantees may depend on the input distribution; a 2026 study establishes conditions and sample bounds for learning compressible distribution families from independently perturbed samples.
openQuestions: Which distribution-dependent guarantees can be estimated from the available observations?
How does structured noise change the relationship between compression and learnability?

papers.title: How many samples are needed to leverage smoothness?
papers.tldr: New generalization-error lower bounds examine how much data is needed before target-function smoothness can deliver its expected learning benefits.

papers.title: Information Theoretic Lower Bounds for Information Theoretic Upper Bounds
papers.tldr: The paper shows why existing mutual-information generalization bounds can miss dimension-independent learning guarantees in stochastic convex optimization.

papers.title: Initialization-Dependent Sample Complexity of Linear Predictors and Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Reference-dependent sample-complexity bounds reveal unexpected behavior in vector-valued prediction and a convex learning problem learnable without uniform convergence.

papers.title: $L_2$-Uniform Stability of Randomized Learning Algorithms: Sharper Generalization Bounds and Confidence Boosting
papers.tldr: L2-uniform stability enables sharper randomized-learning generalization bounds and, through bagging-based confidence boosting, near-optimal high-probability guarantees.

papers.title: Learning via Wasserstein-Based High Probability Generalisation Bounds
papers.tldr: New Wasserstein-based PAC-Bayesian bounds offer high-probability guarantees for potentially heavy-tailed losses and yield optimizable learning objectives.

papers.title: List and Certificate Complexities in Replicable Learning
papers.tldr: The paper establishes achievable and optimal replicability complexities for coin-bias estimation and extends its constructions to statistical-query learning.

papers.title: Minimum Description Length and Generalization Guarantees for Representation Learning
papers.tldr: A compression-based framework bounds representation-learning generalization error and yields informative guarantees even for deterministic encoders.

papers.title: Near-optimal learning with average Hölder smoothness
papers.tldr: Distribution-sensitive average Hölder smoothness yields sharper regression guarantees and nearly optimal algorithms, with matching realizable bounds up to logarithms.

papers.title: On the Convergence of CART under Sufficient Impurity Decrease Condition
papers.tldr: The paper sharpens CART regression error bounds under sufficient impurity decrease and provides conditions for checking when that assumption holds.

papers.title: On the Role of Entanglement and Statistics in Learning
papers.tldr: The paper establishes task-dependent separations between quantum measurement models and introduces a dimension that yields quantum statistical-query lower bounds.

papers.title: Optimal Learners for Realizable Regression: PAC Learning and Online Learning
papers.tldr: New combinatorial dimensions and optimal learners characterize realizable regression in PAC and online settings, while one proposed sufficiency condition remains conjectural.

papers.title: Precise asymptotic generalization for multiclass classification with overparameterized linear models
papers.tldr: Under a growing Gaussian bi-level model, tight bounds identify when multiclass linear classification succeeds or fails and expose limits of minimum-norm interpolation.

papers.title: Tester-Learners for Halfspaces: Universal Algorithms
papers.tldr: A polynomial-time tester-learner guarantees halfspace learning error across a broad distribution class, with stronger results under Massart noise.

papers.title: The Bayesian Stability Zoo
papers.tldr: The paper establishes equivalences within two families of Bayesian stability notions and proves methods for amplifying stability.

papers.title: The Pick-to-Learn Algorithm: Empowering Compression for Tight Generalization Bounds and Improved Post-training Performance
papers.tldr: Pick-to-Learn wraps learning algorithms to obtain compression-based generalization bounds and improves post-training performance in two evaluated settings.

papers.title: Algorithmic Stability Unleashed: Generalization Bounds with Unbounded Losses
papers.tldr: New stability bounds accommodate unbounded losses under subweibull conditions and can improve previous bounds by a square-root-of-sample-size factor.

papers.title: Collaborative Learning with Different Labeling Functions
papers.tldr: Collaborative learning remains sample-efficient under a weaker shared-structure assumption, although general computation is difficult and efficient learners are given for two special cases.

papers.title: Guarantees for Nonlinear Representation Learning: Non-identical Covariates, Dependent Data, Fewer Samples
papers.tldr: The paper establishes guarantees for shared nonlinear representation learning across differing input distributions and possibly dependent observations, with rates matching the independent-data setting.

papers.title: Learning Multiple Secrets in Mastermind
papers.tldr: The paper establishes query algorithms and adaptivity limits for recovering hidden point sets from nearest-point answers.

papers.title: No Dimensional Sampling Coresets for Classification
papers.tldr: A Rademacher-complexity analysis yields classification coresets whose size is independent of input dimension, with extensions to distributional sampling.

papers.title: On a Combinatorial Problem Arising in Machine Teaching
papers.tldr: The paper proves which binary consistency-matrix arrangement gives the worst teaching dimension in a size-based machine-teaching model.

papers.title: On the Minimal Degree Bias in Generalization on the Unseen for non-Boolean Functions
papers.tldr: Minimal-degree generalization depends on the learning regime and token representation, and can fail beyond special non-Boolean embeddings.

papers.title: Position: $C^*$-Algebraic Machine Learning $-$ Moving in a New Direction
papers.tldr: This position paper proposes C*-algebras as a mathematical framework for unifying learning methods and representing richer data.

papers.title: Slicing Mutual Information Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Slicing parameter space yields more tractable generalization bounds, with an extension that connects neural-network compressibility to informative guarantees.

papers.title: Active Learning of General Halfspaces: Label Queries vs Membership Queries
papers.tldr: Under Gaussian inputs, membership queries enable efficient halfspace learning that pool-based label queries cannot generally match without enormous unlabeled pools.

papers.title: Binary Search with Distributional Predictions
papers.tldr: A search algorithm uses full predicted distributions and achieves essentially optimal query complexity tied to target uncertainty and prediction error.

papers.title: Credal Learning Theory
papers.tldr: Credal learning theory generalizes classical risk bounds by representing changing data distributions through convex sets of probabilities.

papers.title: Distribution Learning with Valid Outputs Beyond the Worst-Case
papers.tldr: The paper identifies structured settings where learning a distribution with few invalid outputs requires less effort than worst-case results suggest.

papers.title: Fast Rates for Bandit PAC Multiclass Classification
papers.tldr: A new bandit-feedback classifier removes the multiplicative label-count penalty from the leading accuracy-dependent sample bound in agnostic learning.

papers.title: Generalizablity of Memorization Neural Network
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when memorization networks can generalize, identifying width, sample, and distribution-dependent parameter requirements.

papers.title: Generalization of Hamiltonian algorithms
papers.tldr: A generalization proof method unifies several stochastic learning procedures under absolute-continuity and log-density concentration conditions.

papers.title: Improved Sample Complexity for Multiclass PAC Learning
papers.tldr: The paper tightens multiclass PAC sample-complexity bounds and identifies two open questions whose positive resolution would close further gaps.

papers.title: Learnability of high-dimensional targets by two-parameter models and gradient flow
papers.tldr: Specially constructed two-parameter models can learn high-dimensional targets with high probability, despite unavoidable geometric and representational limits.

papers.title: Learning Noisy Halfspaces with a Margin: Massart is No Harder than Random
papers.tldr: Perspectron improves sample guarantees for learning margin-separated halfspaces under Massart noise and extends to generalized linear models with known links.

papers.title: Learning Partitions from Context
papers.tldr: The paper distinguishes when token classes are identifiable from sparse interactions from when gradient-flow learning can recover them.

papers.title: Learning to Understand: Identifying Interactions via the Möbius Transform
papers.tldr: Sparse, low-degree structure enables more efficient recovery of Möbius interaction coefficients, including a noise-tolerant method connected to group testing.

papers.title: Learning via Surrogate PAC-Bayes
papers.tldr: Surrogate PAC-Bayes replaces expensive risk evaluations with low-dimensional approximations while retaining a theoretical link to optimizing the original generalization bounds.

papers.title: Multiclass Transductive Online Learning
papers.tldr: New combinatorial dimensions characterize transductive online learnability and mistake-rate regimes even with unbounded label sets.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Teaching a Family of Linear Behavior Cloning Learners
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes minimal demonstrations for families of linear behavior-cloning learners and provides an efficient approximation for the NP-hard teaching problem.

papers.title: On the Computational Landscape of Replicable Learning
papers.tldr: The paper establishes computational separations and conversions between replicable, online, and private learning, with explicit conditional and complexity limits.

papers.title: Testably Learning Polynomial Threshold Functions
papers.tldr: Constant-degree polynomial threshold functions admit testable learning guarantees that qualitatively match known agnostic learning runtimes.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Learning RUMs from Small Slates
papers.tldr: With complete choice information, subsets of size proportional to √n are necessary and sufficient for approximate prediction of all Random Utility Model choices.

papers.title: Transductive Learning is Compact
papers.tldr: For broad classes of losses, transductive learnability has exactly the same sample complexity as learnability of every finite projection.

papers.title: Transformation-Invariant Learning and Theoretical Guarantees for OOD Generalization
papers.tldr: The paper gives learning algorithms and sample-complexity guarantees for distribution shifts represented by classes of data transformations.

papers.title: Universal Rates of Empirical Risk Minimization
papers.tldr: In the realizable universal-learning setting, empirical risk minimization has four possible rate categories characterized by concept-class structure.

papers.title: When Is Inductive Inference Possible?
papers.tldr: Inductive inference is possible exactly for hypothesis classes that are countable unions of online-learnable classes, including some uncountable classes.

papers.title: A New Concentration Inequality for Sampling Without Replacement and Its Application for Transductive Learning
papers.tldr: A new concentration inequality enables sharper theoretical guarantees for transductive learning through Transductive Local Complexity.

papers.title: A Trichotomy for List Transductive Online Learning
papers.tldr: The paper proves that realizable list transductive online learning has only three possible mistake-growth rates and characterizes agnostic learnability.

papers.title: Binary Hypothesis Testing for Softmax Models and Leverage Score Models
papers.tldr: The paper bounds the queries needed to distinguish two candidate softmax models and obtains analogous results for leverage-score models.

papers.title: Ehrenfeucht-Haussler Rank and Chain of Thought
papers.tldr: Boolean-function rank exactly characterizes the chain-of-thought steps required by a single-layer hard-attention transformer.

papers.title: Generalization Analysis for Controllable Learning
papers.tldr: A unified theory gives tight generalization bounds for controllable learners, with only logarithmic dependence on the number of task targets.

papers.title: Generalization Analysis for Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning under Non-IID Settings
papers.tldr: The paper derives contrastive-learning generalization bounds that account for dependent tuples formed by reusing labeled examples.

papers.title: Generation from Noisy Examples
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes when generators can eventually produce unseen positive examples despite finitely many hidden negative examples in their input stream.

papers.title: Non-Asymptotic Length Generalization
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes computable guarantees for length generalization in an idealized setting and derives bounds for automata and transformer-related functions.

papers.title: On the Learnability of Distribution Classes with Adaptive Adversaries
papers.tldr: For additive corruption, learning against sample-aware adaptive adversaries is strictly harder than learning against oblivious adversaries.

papers.title: PAC Learning with Improvements
papers.tldr: Allowing people to improve their qualifications can sometimes reduce learning requirements and enable an improvement-aware notion of zero error.

papers.title: Representation Preserving Multiclass Agnostic to Realizable Reduction
papers.tldr: The paper establishes a representation-preserving agnostic-to-realizable reduction for multiclass learning within a framework that also covers list and multilabel learning.

papers.title: Statistical Query Hardness of Multiclass Linear Classification with Random Classification Noise
papers.tldr: Statistical Query lower bounds reveal a sharp increase in noisy linear-classification difficulty when moving from two labels to three or more.

papers.title: The Role of Randomness in Stability
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes the randomness needed for stable learning through deterministic global stability and Littlestone dimension.

papers.title: Agnostic Learning under Targeted Poisoning: Optimal Rates and the Role of Randomness
papers.tldr: The paper establishes optimal agnostic learning rates under targeted poisoning and shows that randomized learners remain effective even when their randomness is visible.

papers.title: Algorithms and SQ Lower Bounds for Robustly Learning Real-valued Multi-Index Models
papers.tldr: The paper gives robust learning algorithms for structured multi-index models and statistical-query lower bounds that nearly match their dependence on input dimension.

papers.title: Computable universal online learning
papers.tldr: The paper shows that universal online learnability need not yield a computable learner and characterizes learnability in additional computable and proper variants.

papers.title: Conservative classifiers do consistently well with improving agents: characterizing statistical and online learning
papers.tldr: Learning theory changes when classified people genuinely improve rather than merely manipulate their features.

papers.title: Efficient PAC Learning for Realizable-Statistic Models via Convex Surrogates
papers.tldr: Suitable convex surrogate losses enable efficient PAC learning with stochastic labels when conditional-label statistics belong to a known function class.

papers.title: How Many Domains Suffice for Domain Generalization? A Tight Characterization via the Domain Shattering Dimension
papers.tldr: The domain shattering dimension tightly characterizes how many randomly sampled domains suffice for learning across a specified domain family.

papers.title: Learning from positive and unlabeled examples -Finite size sample bounds
papers.tldr: The paper bounds the positive and unlabeled sample sizes needed for learning without assuming the positive-class proportion is known.

papers.title: Marginal-Nonuniform PAC Learnability
papers.tldr: A distribution-dependent variant of PAC learning admits a three-way characterization of learning rates based on hypothesis-class structure.

papers.title: Non-Uniform Multiclass Learning with Bandit Feedback
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes non-uniform multiclass learnability and shows that full supervision can enable learning where bandit feedback cannot.

papers.title: On Agnostic PAC Learning in the Small Error Regime
papers.tldr: An efficient aggregation-based learner achieves optimal error rates in the small-error regime, while a sharper leading constant remains open.

papers.title: On Union-Closedness of Language Generation
papers.tldr: The paper proves that combining individually generatable language classes can yield a class that is not generatable.

papers.title: Optimal Mistake Bounds for Transductive Online Learning
papers.tldr: Matching lower and existential upper bounds establish a quadratic possible advantage from advance unlabeled inputs in online learning.

papers.title: Robust Regression of General ReLUs with Queries
papers.tldr: Black-box label queries enable efficient robust learning of general ReLUs with near-optimal query complexity, exceeding what ordinary pool-based active learning can achieve.

papers.title: The Parameterized Complexity of Computing the VC-Dimension
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional hardness bounds for computing VC-dimension and identifies structural parameters that enable faster exact or approximate algorithms.

papers.title: The Power of Iterative Filtering for Supervised Learning with (Heavy) Contamination
papers.tldr: Iterative polynomial filtering enables efficient supervised learning under several contamination models, including heavy contamination under stronger approximation assumptions.

papers.title: Tight Generalization Bounds for Large-Margin Halfspaces
Tighter CMI-Based Generalization Bounds via Stochastic Projection and Quantization
papers.tldr: Projection and compression yield tighter information-based generalization bounds and support the existence of non-memorizing algorithms with comparable generalization.

papers.title: Which Algorithms Have Tight Generalization Bounds?
papers.tldr: Loss stability and conditional variance characterize when algorithms admit tight generalization bounds.

papers.title: A Refined Generalization Analysis for Extreme Multi-class Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning
papers.tldr: New risk estimators give sharper sample-complexity guarantees for supervised contrastive learning with many unevenly represented classes.

papers.title: Conformal C2ST: Turning weak classifiers into strong two-sample tests
papers.tldr: Conformal calibration turns even weak classifier scores into valid two-sample tests whose detection power degrades gently with classifier error.

papers.title: Efficiently Learning Drifting Halfspaces with Massart Noise
papers.tldr: The paper gives an efficient learner for noisy, drifting linear classifiers and evidence of a gap between statistical and computational limits.

papers.title: How Hard Is Science?
papers.tldr: A parameterized analysis of symbolic regression identifies bounded expression complexity as a tractable regime and variable or primitive selection as a source of hardness.

papers.title: Language Generation in the Limit: Complexity Barriers and Implications for Learning
papers.tldr: Sample-complexity barriers separate the theoretical possibility of eventual language generation from its feasibility across several formal language classes.

papers.title: Learning Partial Concept Classes and Universal Rates Under Massart Noise
papers.tldr: Sharper analysis under Massart noise yields new sample-complexity bounds for partial concept classes and completes a characterization of universal learning rates.

papers.title: Length Generalization Bounds for Transformers
papers.tldr: General computable length-generalization bounds are impossible in the studied transformer-linked setting, while fixed-precision transformers admit optimal exponential bounds.

papers.title: Networked Information Aggregation for Binary Classification
papers.tldr: Sequential logit sharing can aggregate distributed classification features under a coverage condition, with network depth constraining achievable excess loss.

papers.title: On Contraction of Sequential and Offset Rademacher Complexities
papers.tldr: Sequential and offset Rademacher complexities admit contraction only with structural conditions and generally unavoidable logarithmic losses.

papers.title: On Learnability and Disambiguation of Multiclass Partial Concept Classes
papers.tldr: Daniely-Shalev dimension characterizes general multiclass partial learnability, and simpler disambiguation labels can unexpectedly make a class unlearnable.

papers.title: Optimal structure learning and conditional independence testing
papers.tldr: For the studied poly-forest settings, optimal conditional independence testing rates determine optimal structure-learning rates.

papers.title: Provable Accuracy Collapse in Embedding-Based Representations under Dimensionality Mismatch
papers.tldr: The paper proves sharp dimensionality barriers for triplet embeddings and a separate computational hardness result conditional on the Unique Games Conjecture.

papers.title: Provable Bounds for the Learnability of Sample-Compressible Families from Noisy Samples
papers.tldr: Sample-compressible distribution families remain learnable under independent additive noise when the paper's necessary and sufficient conditions hold.

papers.title: Realizable Bayes-Consistency for General Metric Losses
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes exactly when realizable learning with general metric losses admits distribution-free, almost-sure convergence to zero risk.

papers.title: Stability beyond Bounded Differences: Sharp Generalization Bounds under Finite $L_p$ Moments
papers.tldr: New concentration results yield sharp stability-based generalization bounds under finite L_p moments, including settings with unbounded losses.

papers.title: Symmetries in PAC-Bayesian Learning
papers.tldr: The paper extends and tightens PAC-Bayesian symmetry guarantees to non-compact transformations and non-invariant data distributions.

papers.title: The Interplay Between Interpolation and Aggregation in Regression: Optimal Sample Complexity
papers.tldr: The median of three interpolating predictors is optimal within a broad aggregation family, but some regression classes require more permissive rules.

papers.title: Tight Margin-Based Generalization Bounds for Voting Classifiers over Finite Hypothesis Sets
papers.tldr: The paper proves an asymptotically tight margin-based generalization bound capturing five interacting factors for voting classifiers.

papers.title: Universal Multiclass Transductive Online Learning
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes transductive online multiclass learnability and shows that learnable classes have bounded or logarithmic optimal mistake rates.
